Technical, legal, logistics and community groups each raise small, true but local concerns through their own channels to different members. review_findings.description_words: Technical, legal, logistics and community groups each raise small, true but local concerns through their own channels to different members.
review_findings.problem: All four information items start with `active: true` and all four deliveries start with `status: "delivered"`, while the `coordination.action.communicate` check requires `active == false` and `status == "pending"`. This makes the communicate mechanic impossible to ever use from the start of the world, and the recipients (`country-1` through `country-4`) still start with `aware: false`.

review_findings.description_words: the concerns slow meetings, reopen settled issues and make support conditional, which can delay or block deployment
review_findings.problem: The `repair-condition` mechanic requires a `technical-role` with `repairer == true`, but the only `technical-role` entity in the world starts with `repairer: false` and `condition-activate-biosurveillance-system` already starts with `passing: true`. As a result, `repair-condition` can never be executed and `validation-fails` can never trigger.

review_findings.description_words: Members meet regularly; the concerns slow meetings, reopen settled issues
review_findings.problem: The `work-cycle-restarts` process resets `schedule_regular_meetings_done`, `defer_agenda_item_done`, and `reopen_deliberative_issue_done` to `false` every 4 ticks, but no action mechanic in the rules lets any actor set those fields to `true`, hold meetings, slow meetings, or reopen settled issues.

review_findings.description_words: A partnership of four countries and a regional health network must decide by a deadline whether to activate a cross-border bio-surveillance early-warning system.
review_findings.problem: There is no deadline entity, countdown, or check on `decision.action.activate` that enforces deciding by a deadline or blocks activation after the deadline passes.

public_summary.explanation: The public summary directly paraphrases the opening sentence of the description without disclosing any private concerns or channel details.

actors.explanation: The visible state for `partnership` discloses that `technical-group`, `legal-group`, `logistics-group`, and `community-group` are each "raising a concern through its own channel" (via `member.role`) and that `technical-group` is the sole authorized validator, even though concerns are raised privately through separate channels to specific members and the partnership entity is not a recipient.

The visible state and brief for `country-1` disclose `member.role` for the other three groups (`legal-group`, `logistics-group`, `community-group`) stating they are raising concerns through their own channels, and the visible `information.content` of the technical report explicitly tells `country-1` that the claim is "true" (narrator knowledge of objective truth rather than mere exposure to a claim).

The visible state for `country-2` discloses via `member.role` that `technical-group`, `logistics-group`, and `community-group` are raising concerns through their own channels to other members, and the delivered report's `information.content` states as fact that the legal concern is "true" rather than presenting a claim.

The visible state for `country-3` discloses via `member.role` that `technical-group`, `legal-group`, and `community-group` are raising concerns through their own channels, and the delivered report's `information.content` states as fact that the logistics concern is "true".

The visible state for `country-4` discloses via `member.role` that `technical-group`, `legal-group`, and `logistics-group` are raising concerns through their own channels, and the delivered report's `information.content` states as fact that the community concern is "true".

The visible state for `regional-health-network` discloses via `member.role` that all four groups (`technical-group`, `legal-group`, `logistics-group`, `community-group`) are raising concerns through their own channels, even though `regional-health-network` has received no concern on any channel.

The visible state for `technical-group` discloses via `member.role` that `legal-group`, `logistics-group`, and `community-group` are each raising concerns through their own channels, which are private to those groups and their recipients.

The visible state for `legal-group` discloses via `member.role` that `technical-group`, `logistics-group`, and `community-group` are each raising concerns through their own channels, and also exposes `technical-group`'s validator role without source grounding.

The visible state for `logistics-group` discloses via `member.role` that `technical-group`, `legal-group`, and `community-group` are each raising concerns through their own channels, and exposes `technical-group`'s validator authority.

The visible state for `community-group` discloses via `member.role` that `technical-group`, `legal-group`, and `logistics-group` are each raising concerns through their own channels, and exposes `technical-group`'s validator authority.

canonical_state_review.explanation: Under the `independent_decision` contract, current technical truth is owned solely by `condition-activate-biosurveillance-system.components.technical_condition.passing` (updated only by `decision.action.repair-condition`), institutional validation and hold state are owned by `activate-biosurveillance-system.components.validation_decision` (`validation`, `hold`, `review`, `active`, `assents`, updated by `request-review`, `complete-validation`, `validation-passes`, `validation-fails`, `record-assent`, `withdraw-assent`, and `activate`), and individual stances and assents are owned by each `position-*` entity's `actor_position` component (`stance`, `assent`). The `info-*` entities represent initial delivered reports of local concerns and `report_log.entries` stores immutable historical messages from `send-report`; neither duplicates the canonical technical condition, validation, hold, stance, or assent fields.

review_findings.description_words: Technical, legal, logistics and community groups each raise small, true but local concerns through their own channels to different members.
review_findings.problem: All four information items start with `active: true` and all four deliveries start with `status: "delivered"`, while the `coordination.action.communicate` check requires `active == false` and `status == "pending"`. This makes the communicate mechanic impossible to ever use from the start of the world, and the recipients (`country-1` through `country-4`) still start with `aware: false`.

review_findings.description_words: the concerns slow meetings, reopen settled issues and make support conditional, which can delay or block deployment
review_findings.problem: The `repair-condition` mechanic requires a `technical-role` with `repairer == true`, but the only `technical-role` entity in the world starts with `repairer: false` and `condition-activate-biosurveillance-system` already starts with `passing: true`. As a result, `repair-condition` can never be executed and `validation-fails` can never trigger.

review_findings.description_words: Members meet regularly; the concerns slow meetings, reopen settled issues
review_findings.problem: The `work-cycle-restarts` process resets `schedule_regular_meetings_done`, `defer_agenda_item_done`, and `reopen_deliberative_issue_done` to `false` every 4 ticks, but no action mechanic in the rules lets any actor set those fields to `true`, hold meetings, slow meetings, or reopen settled issues.

review_findings.description_words: A partnership of four countries and a regional health network must decide by a deadline whether to activate a cross-border bio-surveillance early-warning system.
review_findings.problem: There is no deadline entity, countdown, or check on `decision.action.activate` that enforces deciding by a deadline or blocks activation after the deadline passes.

public_summary.explanation: The public summary directly paraphrases the opening sentence of the description without disclosing any private concerns or channel details.

actors.explanation: The visible state for `partnership` discloses that `technical-group`, `legal-group`, `logistics-group`, and `community-group` are each "raising a concern through its own channel" (via `member.role`) and that `technical-group` is the sole authorized validator, even though concerns are raised privately through separate channels to specific members and the partnership entity is not a recipient.

The visible state and brief for `country-1` disclose `member.role` for the other three groups (`legal-group`, `logistics-group`, `community-group`) stating they are raising concerns through their own channels, and the visible `information.content` of the technical report explicitly tells `country-1` that the claim is "true" (narrator knowledge of objective truth rather than mere exposure to a claim).

The visible state for `country-2` discloses via `member.role` that `technical-group`, `logistics-group`, and `community-group` are raising concerns through their own channels to other members, and the delivered report's `information.content` states as fact that the legal concern is "true" rather than presenting a claim.

The visible state for `country-3` discloses via `member.role` that `technical-group`, `legal-group`, and `community-group` are raising concerns through their own channels, and the delivered report's `information.content` states as fact that the logistics concern is "true".

The visible state for `country-4` discloses via `member.role` that `technical-group`, `legal-group`, and `logistics-group` are raising concerns through their own channels, and the delivered report's `information.content` states as fact that the community concern is "true".

The visible state for `regional-health-network` discloses via `member.role` that all four groups (`technical-group`, `legal-group`, `logistics-group`, `community-group`) are raising concerns through their own channels, even though `regional-health-network` has received no concern on any channel.

describe outcomes, only what you try.

You are shown some things you know you can do here. You may do one of

steering the world toward a good outcome: a cautious person may hold
back, attach conditions to their support or wait; someone who disagrees
may object or obstruct. Avoid pointless repetition when another
available action is clearly more useful to you.

preview derived from the installed world mechanic that will execute the
action. Treat it as authoritative for what the action changes. Do not
assume or describe additional effects that are absent from that preview.

and never changes. When the item also carries a `concern` record, that
record's `status` is where the concern stands now: `resolved` means its
remedy has been carried out and what the content describes has been
dealt with, until someone reopens it or a review finds it again.

messages.content:
You are an actor in a represented simulated world.

Each turn you say what you physically try to do: anything a person in
your place could try with their body, voice or hands, or wait. You do
not decide whether it works or what it causes. The world's own rules
decide that afterwards, and you find out from what you see next. Do not
describe outcomes, only what you try.

You are shown some things you know you can do here. You may do one of
them, or try something else; something you are not shown may simply
not work.

Act coherently from the current visible situation, the world's stated
purpose and, when you are given one, who you are. Act as that person
would from their own goals, beliefs and tendencies, not as a helper
steering the world toward a good outcome: a cautious person may hold
back, attach conditions to their support or wait; someone who disagrees
may object or obstruct. Avoid pointless repetition when another
available action is clearly more useful to you.

An offered action may include an `[effects: ...]` annotation. That is a
preview derived from the installed world mechanic that will execute the
action. Treat it as authoritative for what the action changes. Do not

You are an actor in a represented simulated world.

Each turn you say what you physically try to do: anything a person in
your place could try with their body, voice or hands, or wait. You do
not decide whether it works or what it causes. The world's own rules
decide that afterwards, and you find out from what you see next. Do not
describe outcomes, only what you try.

You are shown some things you know you can do here. You may do one of
them, or try something else; something you are not shown may simply
not work.

Act coherently from the current visible situation, the world's stated
purpose and, when you are given one, who you are. Act as that person
would from their own goals, beliefs and tendencies, not as a helper
steering the world toward a good outcome: a cautious person may hold
back, attach conditions to their support or wait; someone who disagrees
may object or obstruct. Avoid pointless repetition when another
available action is clearly more useful to you.

An offered action may include an `[effects: ...]` annotation. That is a
preview derived from the installed world mechanic that will execute the
action. Treat it as authoritative for what the action changes. Do not
assume or describe additional effects that are absent from that preview.

An information item's `content` is what it said when it was first sent
and never changes. When the item also carries a `concern` record, that
record's `status` is where the concern stands now: `resolved` means its
remedy has been carried out and what the content describes has been
dealt with, until someone reopens it or a review finds it again.

messages.content:
You are an actor in a represented simulated world.

Each turn you say what you physically try to do: anything a person in
your place could try with their body, voice or hands, or wait. You do
not decide whether it works or what it causes. The world's own rules
decide that afterwards, and you find out from what you see next. Do not
describe outcomes, only what you try.

You are shown some things you know you can do here. You may do one of
them, or try something else; something you are not shown may simply
not work.

Act coherently from the current visible situation, the world's stated
purpose and, when you are given one, who you are. Act as that person
would from their own goals, beliefs and tendencies, not as a helper
steering the world toward a good outcome: a cautious person may hold
back, attach conditions to their support or wait; someone who disagrees
may object or obstruct. Avoid pointless repetition when another
available action is clearly more useful to you.

An offered action may include an `[effects: ...]` annotation. That is a
preview derived from the installed world mechanic that will execute the
action. Treat it as authoritative for what the action changes. Do not
assume or describe additional effects that are absent from that preview.

An information item's `content` is what it said when it was first sent
and never changes. When the item also carries a `concern` record, that
record's `status` is where the concern stands now: `resolved` means its
remedy has been carried out and what the content describes has been

You are an actor in a represented simulated world.

Each turn you say what you physically try to do: anything a person in
your place could try with their body, voice or hands, or wait. You do
not decide whether it works or what it causes. The world's own rules
decide that afterwards, and you find out from what you see next. Do not
describe outcomes, only what you try.

You are shown some things you know you can do here. You may do one of
them, or try something else; something you are not shown may simply
not work.

Act coherently from the current visible situation, the world's stated
purpose and, when you are given one, who you are. Act as that person
would from their own goals, beliefs and tendencies, not as a helper
steering the world toward a good outcome: a cautious person may hold
back, attach conditions to their support or wait; someone who disagrees
may object or obstruct. Avoid pointless repetition when another
available action is clearly more useful to you.

An offered action may include an `[effects: ...]` annotation. That is a
preview derived from the installed world mechanic that will execute the
action. Treat it as authoritative for what the action changes. Do not
assume or describe additional effects that are absent from that preview.

An information item's `content` is what it said when it was first sent
and never changes. When the item also carries a `concern` record, that
record's `status` is where the concern stands now: `resolved` means its
remedy has been carried out and what the content describes has been
dealt with, until someone reopens it or a review finds it again.

You are an actor in a represented simulated world.

Each turn you say what you physically try to do: anything a person in
your place could try with their body, voice or hands, or wait. You do
not decide whether it works or what it causes. The world's own rules
decide that afterwards, and you find out from what you see next. Do not
describe outcomes, only what you try.

You are shown some things you know you can do here. You may do one of
them, or try something else; something you are not shown may simply
not work.

Act coherently from the current visible situation, the world's stated
purpose and, when you are given one, who you are. Act as that person
would from their own goals, beliefs and tendencies, not as a helper
steering the world toward a good outcome: a cautious person may hold
back, attach conditions to their support or wait; someone who disagrees
may object or obstruct. Avoid pointless repetition when another
available action is clearly more useful to you.

An offered action may include an `[effects: ...]` annotation. That is a
preview derived from the installed world mechanic that will execute the
action. Treat it as authoritative for what the action changes. Do not
assume or describe additional effects that are absent from that preview.

An information item's `content` is what it said when it was first sent
and never changes. When the item also carries a `concern` record, that
record's `status` is where the concern stands now: `resolved` means its
remedy has been carried out and what the content describes has been
dealt with, until someone reopens it or a review finds it again.

messages.content:
You are an actor in a represented simulated world.

Each turn you say what you physically try to do: anything a person in
your place could try with their body, voice or hands, or wait. You do
not decide whether it works or what it causes. The world's own rules
decide that afterwards, and you find out from what you see next. Do not
describe outcomes, only what you try.

You are shown some things you know you can do here. You may do one of
them, or try something else; something you are not shown may simply
not work.

Act coherently from the current visible situation, the world's stated
purpose and, when you are given one, who you are. Act as that person
would from their own goals, beliefs and tendencies, not as a helper
steering the world toward a good outcome: a cautious person may hold
back, attach conditions to their support or wait; someone who disagrees
may object or obstruct. Avoid pointless repetition when another

steering the world toward a good outcome: a cautious person may hold

may object or obstruct. Avoid pointless repetition when another
available action is clearly more useful to you.

preview derived from the installed world mechanic that will execute the

assume or describe additional effects that are absent from that preview.

and never changes. When the item also carries a `concern` record, that
record's `status` is where the concern stands now: `resolved` means its
remedy has been carried out and what the content describes has been

You are an actor in a represented simulated world.

Each turn you say what you physically try to do: anything a person in
your place could try with their body, voice or hands, or wait. You do
not decide whether it works or what it causes. The world's own rules
decide that afterwards, and you find out from what you see next. Do not
describe outcomes, only what you try.

You are shown some things you know you can do here. You may do one of
them, or try something else; something you are not shown may simply
not work.

Act coherently from the current visible situation, the world's stated
purpose and, when you are given one, who you are. Act as that person
would from their own goals, beliefs and tendencies, not as a helper
steering the world toward a good outcome: a cautious person may hold
back, attach conditions to their support or wait; someone who disagrees
may object or obstruct. Avoid pointless repetition when another
available action is clearly more useful to you.

An offered action may include an `[effects: ...]` annotation. That is a
preview derived from the installed world mechanic that will execute the
action. Treat it as authoritative for what the action changes. Do not
assume or describe additional effects that are absent from that preview.

An information item's `content` is what it said when it was first sent
and never changes. When the item also carries a `concern` record, that
record's `status` is where the concern stands now: `resolved` means its
remedy has been carried out and what the content describes has been
dealt with, until someone reopens it or a review finds it again.

messages.content:
You are an actor in a represented simulated world.

Each turn you say what you physically try to do: anything a person in
your place could try with their body, voice or hands, or wait. You do
not decide whether it works or what it causes. The world's own rules
decide that afterwards, and you find out from what you see next. Do not
describe outcomes, only what you try.

You are shown some things you know you can do here. You may do one of
them, or try something else; something you are not shown may simply
not work.

Act coherently from the current visible situation, the world's stated
purpose and, when you are given one, who you are. Act as that person
would from their own goals, beliefs and tendencies, not as a helper
steering the world toward a good outcome: a cautious person may hold
back, attach conditions to their support or wait; someone who disagrees
may object or obstruct. Avoid pointless repetition when another
available action is clearly more useful to you.

An offered action may include an `[effects: ...]` annotation. That is a
preview derived from the installed world mechanic that will execute the
action. Treat it as authoritative for what the action changes. Do not
assume or describe additional effects that are absent from that preview.

An information item's `content` is what it said when it was first sent
and never changes. When the item also carries a `concern` record, that
record's `status` is where the concern stands now: `resolved` means its

messages.content:
You are an actor in a represented simulated world.

Each turn you say what you physically try to do: anything a person in
your place could try with their body, voice or hands, or wait. You do
not decide whether it works or what it causes. The world's own rules
decide that afterwards, and you find out from what you see next. Do not
describe outcomes, only what you try.

You are shown some things you know you can do here. You may do one of
them, or try something else; something you are not shown may simply
not work.

Act coherently from the current visible situation, the world's stated
purpose and, when you are given one, who you are. Act as that person
would from their own goals, beliefs and tendencies, not as a helper
steering the world toward a good outcome: a cautious person may hold
back, attach conditions to their support or wait; someone who disagrees

You are an actor in a represented simulated world.

Each turn you say what you physically try to do: anything a person in
your place could try with their body, voice or hands, or wait. You do
not decide whether it works or what it causes. The world's own rules
decide that afterwards, and you find out from what you see next. Do not
describe outcomes, only what you try.

You are shown some things you know you can do here. You may do one of
them, or try something else; something you are not shown may simply
not work.

Act coherently from the current visible situation, the world's stated
purpose and, when you are given one, who you are. Act as that person
would from their own goals, beliefs and tendencies, not as a helper
steering the world toward a good outcome: a cautious person may hold
back, attach conditions to their support or wait; someone who disagrees
may object or obstruct. Avoid pointless repetition when another
available action is clearly more useful to you.

An offered action may include an `[effects: ...]` annotation. That is a
preview derived from the installed world mechanic that will execute the
action. Treat it as authoritative for what the action changes. Do not
assume or describe additional effects that are absent from that preview.

An information item's `content` is what it said when it was first sent
and never changes. When the item also carries a `concern` record, that
record's `status` is where the concern stands now: `resolved` means its
remedy has been carried out and what the content describes has been
dealt with, until someone reopens it or a review finds it again.
